entire checkpoint search — Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using semantic and keyword matching
Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using hybrid search (semantic + keyword),
powered by the Entire search service.

Requires authentication via 'entire login' (GitHub device flow).

By default, results are scoped to the current repository. Use --all-repos to
search across all accessible repos.

Run without arguments to open an interactive search. Results are
displayed in an interactive table. Use --json for machine-readable output,
and add --compact for a trimmed per-result shape suited to agents (implies
--json): id, type, repo, branch, author, date, files touched, score, match
snippet, and a truncated title instead of the full prompt (repo hits add
description and checkpoint count). Fetch full detail
for a single result with 'entire checkpoint explain <id>', or add --full to
that command to pull the checkpoint's entire session transcript. For a
checkpoint hit from another GitHub repo, add --repo <owner/name> to
'entire checkpoint explain' (requires the full checkpoint ID; unrelated to
this command's --repo filter below).

CLI queries also support inline filters like author:<name>, date:<week|month>,
branch:<name>, repo:<owner/name>, and repo:* to search all accessible repos.

Examples:
entire checkpoint search "retry backoff" --json
  entire checkpoint search "retry backoff" --json --compact
  entire checkpoint search "auth timeout author:alice date:week"
  entire checkpoint search --code "parseToken"

  "body": "Problem: Trail commands currently target the control-plane BFF for all operations, but the new production backend (entire-api) uses different conventions: camelCase instead of snake_case, cursor pagination instead of offset/limit, repo/number addressing instead of trail ID, and uses 204 No Content for deletion instead of a response body.\nSolution: Migrate trail commands to route directly to the entire-api cell that owns the repository. The changes include:\nAutomatic payload normalization: New normalizeLegacyTrailJSON() and custom UnmarshalJSON() methods on response types transparently convert between snake_case (BFF/test fixtures) and camelCase (entire-api) so both formats work seamlessly.\nCursor-based pagination: Replace offset/limit with opaque page tokens and cursor pagination. The server page cap changed from 200 to 100 rows. The pagination logic now walks multiple pages to reach the requested limit.\nRoute mapping: Store a trail ID → repo/number path mapping in the API client so review helpers (which work internally with trail IDs) can transparently hit the native entire-api routes.\nDirect cell routing: Trail commands now call newTrailAPIClient() to resolve the owning entire-api cell by repository, instead of going through the BFF. This uses the same cluster-lookup logic as other repo-scoped commands.\nDeletion acknowledgement: Accept HTTP 204 No Content as the success signal for trail deletion instead of checking {ok: true} in the response.\nSSE event normalization: Review stream events are also normalized from snake_case to camelCase, with special handling for the payload field which stays unchanged for backward compatibility.\nAll tests are updated to match the new format and pagination model. Backward compatibility is maintained for cached/test payloads via the normalization layer.",
